---
title: "How do I draw a boxplot and identify potential outliers?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I draw a boxplot and identify potential outliers?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Confirm the values are numeric.

2. Draw boxplot() and label the units.

3. Inspect boxplot.stats() and explain its flagged points.

## Runnable example

```{r}
x <- c(3,4,5,5,6,6,7,7,8,8,9,31)
boxplot(x,col="#CEE2F0",border="#244967",ylab="Depth (cm)",
        main="Distribution of depths")
s <- boxplot.stats(x)
print(s$out)
legend("topright",legend=paste("Median =",median(x)),bty="n")
```

## Interpret the result

The box shows the middle half and median. The separate flagged observation should be checked against the original measurement, not deleted without evidence.

## Check before applying to real data

Boxplot outliers are values outside the default 1.5 x IQR fences, not automatically measurement errors.
